title: Application of lidocaine gel via subglottic secretion drainage during spontaneous awakening trials - a randomized double-blind cross-over study (LIDSAT)
summary:
Patients need to be ventilated in an intensive care unit for various reasons. This is done through a breathing tube (tube), which lies through the mouth, throat, vocal folds in the trachea. In order for patients to tolerate this tube and not to press pressure against the ventilator, they are sedated. To check whether the patient wakes up adequately and whether we can remove the breathing tube, we reduce the sedatives once a day so that the patient wakes up under controlled conditions. We refer to this as a spontaneous awakening trial. Sometimes patients react with stress, press against the ventilator, the heartbeat becomes faster, and blood pressure rises. Then the procedure is stopped without to check whether the patient shows adequate reactions and whether the breathing tube can be removed. 
With this study, we now want to investigate whether we can improve this situation by administering an anesthetic gel (lidocaingel).  The gel is administered via a thin tube that is integrated into the breathing tube. Saliva residues in the area of the vocal folds are normally sucked out via this tube to prevent pneumonia. The anesthetic gel reduces the irritation of the breathing tube. We hope that this will reduce the amount of pressing against the ventilator and make it easier for the patient to be evaluated neurologically.

interventions.name: Application of 5 ml lidocaine gel 2% via subglottic secretion drainage  prior to the start  and repeat after 20 minutes
Placebo control group: Application of 5ml sodium chloride 0.9% via subglottic secretion drainage prior to the start and repeat after 20 minutes

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• spontaneous awakening trial indicated
• consent available (health care representative/supervisor)
• endotracheal tube with  subglottic secretion drainage present
• sedation: isoflurane and remifentanil
• esophageal pressure probe available
Exclusion criteria:
• immediate extubation planned
• malignant hyperthermia
• increased intracranial pressure
• acute CNS disease in the last 14 days
• extreme hemodynamic instabilityt
• ECMO
• patients who are permanently incapable of giving consent
• lidocaine allergy
• isolation in case of Covid/open tuberculosis infection
• no placement of the esophageal pressure probe possible (e.g. chest stomach)
